critique: The mechanism-loss theorem proves a sharp lower envelope for the optimized regret ratio and characterizes equality, but it does not give the exact general-K ratio except when its support-and-normalized-vector condition holds. The general-K value is only existentially certified: no executed transcript or optimized three-policy risk is delivered, so the displayed three-policy arithmetic verifies the hit matrix but not the advertised numerical design computation. The primitive LAN lower bounds are stated for fixed allocations, while no single theorem establishes the optimized primitive minimax identity uniformly over allocation sequences; accordingly, the framing should not imply more than the proved Gaussian-design comparison and transferred achievability. The closest theorem-text comparator is the public [Han–Owusu–Shin arXiv preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18590), while the Chan comparator is a nonarchival poster and supplies no load-bearing priority comparison.
